7500472122528641024.author: Ignacio Ibeas

Memory, not compute, is the true rate limiter of the Agentic era.

While the world remains fixated on GPU compute clusters, artificial intelligence is running headfirst into a massive physical barrier: the memory wall.

🧠 The Collapse of the Classical Model
For over half a century, computing has operated under the classical Von Neumann architecture—a clean, physical division between the compute processor (the "head") and memory storage (the "tape").

That model worked when software memory demands were modest. But frontier transformer models have upended the paradigm:

Stripe just paid $7B for OpenRouter. NVIDIA paid $12.9B for Hugging Face.

Neither company makes models. So why the eye-watering multiples?

Because they own the front door. OpenRouter is where developers choose a model. Hugging Face is where they pull model weights. Owning that top of funnel means seeing demand and usage trends before anyone else. And both of their successes are tied to the rise of open weight models, a trend that has only accelerated as enterprises push to cut token costs.

NVIDIA’s real moat is not the GPU.
 
It is CUDA and the software ecosystem around it.
 
The hardware lead matters, but the switching costs for AI/ML teams are now so high that they function as a structural barrier. Once a company has built its stack, tooling, kernels, and internal expertise around CUDA, moving is not a procurement decision. It is an organizational and technical rewrite with real timeline and performance risk.

7500708121590394880.author: Kevin Selhi
7500708121590394880.text: Congrats to the Wafer team! They use AI to optimize model inference specific to the hardware it's executed on. NVIDIA's advantages are many and CUDA is high on the list. But as AI adoption and utilization increase, one firm won't be able to satisfy all the world's demand for compute. To fulfill AI's promise, inference providers will increasingly need to run models on non-NVIDIA hardware (i.e. AMD's family of chips, Google TPUs, Cerebras, Etched, Positron, etc). Looking forward to a world where >1k tokens per second is the norm. Thankfully Emilio Andere, Eugene Ye, JV Cosico and their team are laser focused on getting us there, sooner than later.
